close_reason: Landed in c430f73. Added PartialEq<str>, PartialEq<&str>, Borrow<str> impls on Sha256 mirroring the sibling jmap-types::Id newtype surface. Three new unit tests exercise the impls with independent string oracles. HashMap<Sha256, V>::get(&str) now compiles. Inline comment block on the impls cites the bd:JMAP-sf5h.7 From-asymmetry rationale.
description: Cookie-cutter inconsistency: jmap-types::Id, UTCDate, Date, State all carry PartialEq<str>, PartialEq<&str>, and Borrow<str> via the impl_string_newtype! macro (see crate-jmap-types/src/id.rs:72-116). jmap-cid-types::Sha256 omits all three. Practical impact: 'sha256 == "e3b0..."' does not compile; you must write 'sha256.as_str() == "e3b0..."'. HashMap<Sha256, V>::get(&str) does not compile without Borrow<str>. Caller-side this is a small papercut but per workspace AGENTS.md 'Canonical Templates' the type crates are deliberately cookie-cutter — every wire-format newtype should look like every other one. Suggested rewrite: add the four impls inline in digest.rs (not via the jmap-types macro — Sha256 is in a sibling crate; copy the pattern). Carry a // ABNF-validated newtype, sibling-of-Id shape doc comment so future readers know the consistency is intentional. Section 7 note: this is NOT 'opinion' — the macro pattern is documented at the workspace canonical-templates level and applies across the type family.
title: Sha256 lacks PartialEq<str> / PartialEq<&str> / Borrow<str> impls vs. sibling jmap-types Id newtype
